minutes.headline: Water commissioners declined to decide on a developer's request to extend a water main outside the district, pending a housing appeals ruling.
minutes.summary: A developer asked the board to allow a water main extension about 500 feet outside the district boundary, citing the 1939 act and prior counsel opinions. One commissioner said no, citing the voters and the attorney; another would not answer until the Housing Appeals Committee rules, and the third member was absent. The board promised a more definitive answer at its next meeting. Commissioners also discussed PFAS levels in wells and a backup power need.

public_comment.topic: A resident argued district expansion must come from the district's voters, who have already voted, and that this proposal circumvents that.
A resident asked what the HAC is and a speaker explained it is the Housing Appeals Committee.
A resident questioned why the Town of Lunenburg was not told of the meeting although it is a party to the 40B action.

budget_items.what_was_said: A commissioner said he did not want to spend more money on legal fees.
A speaker said the Hickory Hills well is available for funding and treatment, and pushed to get the treatment plant built.

Board to give a more definitive answer at its next meeting, April 12th.

what_happened.line: The water commissioners made no decision on a developer's request to extend a water main outside the district boundary; the third commissioner was absent.
The board said it would give a more definitive answer at its next meeting, April 12th.
One commissioner opposed the extension, citing the district's voters and the attorney; another would not answer until the Housing Appeals Committee rules.
A resident argued that expanding the district must come from the district's voters, who have already voted, and that the proposal circumvents that.
Commissioners also discussed PFAS in the wells, funding for treatment at the Hickory Hills well, and a need for backup power.

why_it_matters: Whether the district's pipes can serve land outside its boundary is tied to a pending housing appeals case, and the answer affects who is served and who pays for the water system.
PFAS treatment funding and the backup power need are costs the district may ask its ratepayers to carry or seek outside money for.
